property_summary: Calling deposit should never revert for any nonnegative msg.value (i.e., deposit must accept any sent value without reverting).

For any positive deposit amount sent to deposit, the call must not revert (i.e., deposit reverts only when msg.value == 0).

For every deposit call, the contract preserves the invariant that depositing a non-zero amount strictly increases the caller's recorded balance (balances[msg.sender] after deposit > before deposit); the mutant removing the assert allows zero-value deposits (and would also mask overflow checks) so this invariant can be violated for some fuzzed amount (e.g., zero).

For every depositor and deposit amount, if the contract receives a positive msg.value then the depositor's recorded balance strictly increases by that positive amount; the mutant that removes the assert allows accepting zero-value deposits which can leave the recorded balance unchanged for a zero deposit, violating the strict-increase rule for some fuzz inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount, after calling deposit() the contract's recorded balance for that caller equals the previous recorded balance plus msg.value (i.e. balances[msg] increases by exactly msg.value); the mutant removing the assert can accept a zero-value deposit and leave balances unchanged relative to expectations when msg.value == 0, or in presence of overflow the assert in reference prevents wrapping — the rule enforces balances[msg] == old + msg.value for all admissible inputs and the mutant can violate it for some fuzzed amount.

For any caller and any deposit value, the reference contract never accepts a zero-value deposit (it asserts to prevent deposits with msg.value == 0 or overflow), so deposit() either reverts for msg.value == 0 or increases the recorded balance; the mutant removing the assert will accept zero-value deposits and thus can leave balances unchanged allowing a successful deposit call that doesn't change address(c).balance or the depositor's balance mapping in the same way the reference forbids.

For any caller and any msg.value, if deposit() returns (does not revert) then the contract's recorded per-caller balance equals the contract's previous per-caller balance plus msg.value (i.e. balances[caller] after == before + msg.value); the mutant (which removes the assert) allows a scenario where deposit() succeeds but balances do not increase by msg.value (notably when msg.value == 0), thus violating this rule for some fuzzed inputs.
